definition_zh: 阅读；朗读；理解；显示
definition_en: to look at and understand written words; to say written words aloud; to interpret or understand a situation; to show a measurement, of an instrument
core_image: 灯光下一页翻开、字行清晰的书
scene: 台灯下，书页被轻轻翻开，一行行字在光里清清楚楚。She read the letter twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里 read 是「阅读」（第 1 个义项：看文字并理解其意思）；句意为她把信读了两遍才回复。画面里可留意：台灯的光、翻开的书页、清晰的字行。

derivatives.zh: read 加 -er，指读者、读本
read 加 -ing，指阅读、读数
read 加 -able，指可读的、易读的
read 与 out 复合，指读数显示

senses.title: To understand written words
senses.definition: to look at written or printed words and understand their meaning
senses.definitionCN: 看书面或印刷的文字并理解其意思
senses.example: She read the letter twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信读了两遍才回复。
senses.why: Old English rædan meant to interpret and advise, and understanding written marks is a form of interpreting them.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 rædan 意为解释与建议，而理解书写的符号正是解释它们的一种方式。

senses.title: To say aloud
senses.definition: to speak written words aloud, especially to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 把书面文字大声说出，尤指读给听众
senses.example: He read the poem to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他给全班朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Reading aloud adds the voice to the act of understanding, so the same verb covers both silent and spoken reading.
senses.whyCN: 朗读在理解的动作上加了声音，于是同一个动词既指默读，也指出声读。

senses.title: To interpret
senses.definition: to understand or judge a situation, a person or a sign in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式理解或判断形势、人或迹象
senses.example: She read his silence as disapproval.
senses.exampleCN: 她把他的沉默理解为不赞成。
senses.why: Because reading is interpreting marks, the verb naturally extends to interpreting anything that carries a meaning.
senses.whyCN: 既然阅读就是解释符号，这个动词便自然扩展到解释任何携带意义之物。

senses.title: To show a measurement
senses.definition: of an instrument, to show a particular figure or value
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器显示出某个数字或数值
senses.example: The thermometer read thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示三十度。
senses.why: An instrument's dial is like a line of writing that must be read, so the verb came to mean what a gauge shows.
senses.whyCN: 仪器的表盘就像一行需要读取的文字，于是这个动词也指仪表所显示的内容。

intro.en: Read is a native English word from Old English rædan, to advise, interpret or read, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: read 是英语本族词，来自古英语 rædan（劝告、解释、阅读），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Rædan meant to advise, interpret or explain, and reading written marks was one kind of interpretation.
items.cn: rædan 意为劝告、解释或说明，而阅读书写符号是解释的一种。

items.en: Related Germanic words tie the verb to counsel and to the solving of a riddle.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语词把这个动词与劝告、猜解谜语联系起来。

items.en: Middle English read narrowed toward the reading of texts, while the older sense of counsel faded.
items.cn: 中古英语 read 向「读文本」收窄，较早的「劝告」之义逐渐消失。

items.en: The verb grew to cover reading aloud and interpreting signs, since both are ways of giving meaning to marks.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到朗读与解读迹象，因为两者都是赋予符号意义的方式。

items.en: Modern English uses read for texts, for spoken reading, for interpreting situations, and for what gauges show.
items.cn: 现代英语用 read 指文本、出声读、解读形势，以及仪表所显示的内容。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of studying, scanning and interpreting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与复合词；近义组收表示研读、浏览与解读的动词。

entries.definition: The act of reading, or a figure shown.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读的行为，或显示的数值。

entries.definition: To read and learn about a subject.
To explain the meaning of something.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as interpreting marks, then covers silent reading, reading aloud, reading a situation, and reading a gauge.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「解释符号」开始，随后涵盖默读、朗读、解读形势与读取仪表。

normal.en: Read a book and read a situation use the same verb because both mean interpreting signs.
normal.cn: read a book 与 read a situation 用同一个动词，因为两者都是解释符号。

normal.en: Read aloud adds a voice to the act of understanding written words.
normal.cn: read aloud 在理解文字的动作上加了声音。

normal.en: Read between the lines means to find meaning that is not written down.
normal.cn: read between the lines 意为找出没有明写的含义。

normal.en: A gauge reads a figure the way a page reads a sentence.
normal.cn: 仪表 reads 一个数字，就像书页 reads 一句话。

normal.en: Reader and reading come straight from read, one for the person and one for the act.
normal.cn: reader 与 reading 直接来自 read，一个指人，一个指行为。

abstract.en: To read is to let marks become meaning.
abstract.cn: read 就是让符号变成意义。

abstract.en: What we read in a silence says more about us than about the silence.
abstract.cn: 我们从沉默中读到的东西，更多说明我们自己，而不是沉默。

abstract.en: Every reading is a choice of which marks to notice.
abstract.cn: 每一次阅读都是在选择注意哪些符号。

examples.en: She read the letter twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把信读了两遍才回复。

examples.en: He read the poem to the class.
examples.cn: 他给全班朗读了这首诗。

examples.en: The thermometer read thirty degrees.
examples.cn: 温度计显示三十度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞德」——台灯下翻开的书页，字行清清楚楚，记住 read 是阅读、朗读。

root: 古英语 rædan（劝告、解释、阅读）→ 中古英语 read → 现代英语 read；同族有 reader、reading、readable、readout。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is interpreting marks; the senses divide into reading text, reading aloud, interpreting a situation, and reading a gauge.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「解释符号」；义项分为阅读文本、朗读、解读形势，以及读取仪表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page opened under a lamp, its lines clear in the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下一页翻开的书，字行在光里清清楚楚。

branches.en: a letter read twice before a reply
a poem spoken to a class
silence taken as disapproval
branches.cn: 被理解为不赞成的沉默

branches.en: a thermometer showing thirty degrees
reading words and reading signs

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其词族由英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 读者；读本；读取器；审稿人
definition_en: a person who reads; a book of texts for learning a language or subject; a device that reads data; a person who reads and comments on manuscripts
core_image: 图书馆窗边低头翻书的人
scene: 图书馆的窗边，一个人低着头，一页页翻着手中的书。The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
sceneCN: 这里 reader 是「读者」（第 1 个义项：阅读书刊的人）；句意为这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。画面里可留意：窗边的座位、低头翻书的人、摊开的书页。

pos.zh: 读者；读本；读取器；审稿人

derivatives.zh: reader 去掉 -er，指阅读
read 加 -ing，指阅读、读数
read 加 -able，指可读的、易读的
reader 加 -ship，指读者群、读者人数

senses.title: A person who reads
senses.definition: a person who reads books, magazines or other texts
senses.definitionCN: 阅读书籍、杂志或其他文本的人
senses.example: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。
senses.why: Reader is simply read plus the agent ending -er, so it names the one who performs the act of reading.
senses.whyCN: reader 就是 read 加施动词尾 -er，因此它命名的是执行阅读这一动作的人。

senses.title: A book for learning
senses.definition: a book containing texts chosen for learning a language or a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为学习语言或某科目而编选的文本汇编
senses.example: The class worked through a French reader.
senses.exampleCN: 全班学完了一本法语读本。
senses.why: A book made to be read by learners was called a reader, because the book itself is meant for reading practice.
senses.whyCN: 为学习者编的书被称为 reader，因为这本书本身就是供阅读练习用的。

senses.title: A device that reads data
senses.definition: a machine or device that reads information from cards, discs or codes
senses.definitionCN: 从卡片、光盘或代码中读取信息的机器或装置
senses.example: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。
senses.why: The agent ending was extended to machines, since a device that reads data performs the same act as a person reading it.
senses.whyCN: 施动词尾被扩展到机器，因为读取数据的装置与读数据的人执行同一个动作。

senses.title: A manuscript reviewer
senses.definition: a person employed to read and comment on manuscripts for a publisher
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为出版社阅读并评议稿件的人
senses.example: The manuscript was sent to an outside reader.
senses.exampleCN: 稿子被送给一位外审。
senses.why: In publishing, the person who reads a manuscript before it is accepted performs the act of reading as a job, hence the title reader.
senses.whyCN: 在出版业，接受前阅读稿子的人以阅读为职业，因此得到 reader 这个称号。

intro.en: Reader is formed in English from the verb read and the agent ending -er, and the verb itself goes back to Old English rædan.
intro.cn: reader 由英语动词 read 与施动词尾 -er 构成，而这个动词可追溯到古英语 rædan。

items.en: Old English had rædere for a reader or interpreter, formed from rædan, to read or explain.
items.cn: 古英语已有 rædere，指读者或解释者，由 rædan（阅读、解释）构成。

items.en: The ending -er marks the one who does an action, so read plus -er is the one who reads.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 标记执行动作的人，因此 read 加 -er 就是阅读的人。

items.en: Middle English reader kept the sense of a person who reads and began to name books meant for reading practice.
items.cn: 中古英语 reader 保留「阅读的人」之意，并开始指供阅读练习的书。

items.en: Modern use extended the word to machines that read data and to people paid to read manuscripts.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到读取数据的机器，以及受雇阅读稿件的人。

items.en: Modern English uses reader for the person, the learning book, the device and the manuscript reviewer.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reader 指人、学习读本、读取器与审稿人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on read; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who receive texts.
note.cn: 形近组收由 read 构成的形式；近义组收表示接收文本的人。

entries.definition: The collective readers of a publication.
The people reached by a book, film or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 书、电影或演讲所触及的人群。

entries.definition: A person who pays to receive a publication.
entries.definitionCN: 付费订阅某出版物的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is read plus -er, and the ending has stretched from people to books, machines and manuscript reviewers.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 read 加 -er，这个词尾已从人扩展到书、机器与审稿人。

normal.en: Reader is read plus -er, so it names whoever or whatever does the reading.
normal.cn: reader 是 read 加 -er，命名做阅读的人或物。

normal.en: A regular reader comes back to the same magazine issue after issue.
normal.cn: regular reader 一期又一期地回到同一本杂志。

normal.en: A graded reader is a book written at a controlled level for learners.
normal.cn: graded reader 是按受控难度为学习者写的书。

normal.en: A card reader reads the stripe on a card the way a person reads a page.
normal.cn: card reader 读卡片上的磁条，就像人读书页。

normal.en: Readership is the whole body of readers taken together.
normal.cn: readership 是把全体读者合在一起看。

abstract.en: A reader is not a passive receiver but a maker of meaning.
abstract.cn: 读者不是被动的接收者，而是意义的制作者。

abstract.en: Every text has as many readers as it has readings.
abstract.cn: 每个文本有多少种读法，就有多少个读者。

abstract.en: To be a good reader is to notice what the text leaves out.
abstract.cn: 做一个好读者，就是注意到文本省略了什么。

examples.en: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
examples.cn: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。

examples.en: The class worked through a French reader.
examples.cn: 全班学完了一本法语读本。

examples.en: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
examples.cn: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「窗边翻书的人」——read 加 -er 就是读者，记住 reader 是读者、读本。

root: 古英语 rædan（阅读、解释）→ 英语 read + 施动后缀 -er → reader；同族有 read、reading、readable、readership。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one who reads; the senses divide into a person, a learning book, a reading device, and a manuscript reviewer.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「阅读者」；义项分为人、学习读本、读取装置与审稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure by a library window, head down, turning one page after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：图书馆窗边的一个人，低头一页页翻书。

branches.en: a reader by a library window
a graded reader on a school desk
a card sliding through a reader
a manuscript handed to an outside reader
a person reading and a machine reading

intro.en: The word is built in English from a native verb and a productive agent ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由本族动词与一个能产的施动词尾在英语中构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 乐意地；容易地；随时可用地
definition_en: willingly and without hesitation; easily and without difficulty; in a way that is available at hand
core_image: 工具摆在手边，一伸手就能拿到
scene: 工具都摆在工作台手边，需要时一伸手就能拿到。She readily agreed to help.
sceneCN: 这里 readily 是「乐意地」（第 1 个义项：毫不犹豫地愿意）；句意为她欣然同意帮忙。画面里可留意：摆在工作台手边的工具、伸出的手。

pos.zh: 乐意地；容易地；随时可用地

derivatives.zh: readily 去掉 -ly，指准备好的、乐意的
ready 加 -ness，指准备就绪、乐意
ready 与 made 复合，指现成的

senses.title: Willingly
senses.definition: willingly and without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 愿意且毫不犹豫
senses.example: She readily agreed to help.
senses.exampleCN: 她欣然同意帮忙。
senses.why: Readily is ready with the adverb ending, and ready already meant prepared, so the adverb says the mind is prepared to say yes.
senses.whyCN: readily 是 ready 加副词词尾，而 ready 本就意为「准备好」，因此这个副词说心已准备好答应。

senses.title: Easily
senses.definition: easily, without difficulty or delay
senses.definitionCN: 轻而易举、没有困难或拖延
senses.example: The information is readily understood by beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 初学者也能轻易理解这些信息。
senses.why: What is ready at hand is also easy to use, so the word passed from willingness to ease of doing.
senses.whyCN: 手边现成之物也便于使用，于是这个词从「乐意」转到「容易」。

senses.title: At hand
senses.definition: in a state of being available whenever needed
senses.definitionCN: 处于需要时随时可用的状态
senses.example: Clean water is readily available in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市里干净的水随时可得。
senses.why: The oldest sense of ready is prepared, and what is prepared is already there when wanted, hence readily available.
senses.whyCN: ready 最古老的意思就是「准备好」，准备好的东西在需要时已经在那里，因此有了 readily available。

intro.en: Readily is ready with the adverb ending -ly; ready goes back to Old English ræde, prepared, from rædan, to arrange or advise.
intro.cn: readily 是 ready 加副词词尾 -ly；ready 可追溯到古英语 ræde（准备好的），源自动词 rædan（安排、劝告）。

items.en: Ræde meant prepared or ready, of a person or a thing made fit for use.
items.cn: ræde 意为准备好的，指人或物已被安排得适于使用。

items.en: Middle English kept ready for what is prepared, and extended it to a willing mind.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 ready 表示「准备好的」，并把它扩展到乐意的态度。

items.en: The ending -ly turned ready into readily, meaning in a ready manner.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把 ready 变成 readily，意为以准备好的方式。

items.en: A mind ready to agree is a mind that agrees readily, and a thing ready at hand is one used readily.
items.cn: 准备好同意的心，就是欣然同意的心；手边现成之物，就是容易使用之物。

items.en: Modern English uses readily for willing agreement, for easy understanding, and for what is available at hand.
items.cn: 现代英语用 readily 指乐意的同意、容易的理解，以及手边可得之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers ready forms and one confusable adverb; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of willingness and ease.
note.cn: 形近组收 ready 的形式与一个易混副词；近义组收表示意愿与容易的副词。

entries.definition: Made in advance and available at once.

normalIntro.en: The adverb draws on ready as prepared: prepared to agree is willing, prepared at hand is easy, prepared in advance is available.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词取 ready「准备好」之意：准备好同意就是乐意，准备好手边就是容易，预先准备好就是随时可用。

normal.en: Readily is ready with -ly, so it says something is done in a ready manner.
normal.cn: readily 是 ready 加 -ly，说明某事以准备好的方式完成。

normal.en: She readily agreed means she was ready to say yes.
normal.cn: She readily agreed 意为她准备好答应。

normal.en: Readily available means the thing is already there when you need it.
normal.cn: readily available 意为需要时东西已经在那里。

normal.en: What is readily understood is understood without effort.
normal.cn: readily understood 之物，理解起来不费力。

normal.en: Ready and already look alike, but already means before now.
normal.cn: ready 与 already 形近，但 already 意为「在此之前」。

abstract.en: Readily measures the distance between a need and an answer.
abstract.cn: readily 衡量的是需求与答案之间的距离。

abstract.en: A thing readily given may still be carefully chosen.
abstract.cn: 乐意给出的东西，也可能是经过仔细选择的。

abstract.en: The easier something is to use, the more readily it is used.
abstract.cn: 某物越容易使用，就越常被使用。

examples.en: She readily agreed to help.
examples.cn: 她欣然同意帮忙。

examples.en: The information is readily understood by beginners.
examples.cn: 初学者也能轻易理解这些信息。

examples.en: Clean water is readily available in the city.
examples.cn: 这座城市里干净的水随时可得。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「工具摆在手边」——伸手就能拿，随时能用，记住 readily 是乐意地、容易地。

root: 古英语 rædan（安排、劝告）→ ræde（准备好的）→ 英语 ready + 副词后缀 -ly → readily；同族有 ready、readiness、ready-made。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being prepared; the senses divide into a willing mind, an easy action, and a thing at hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「已准备好」；义项分为乐意的心、容易的动作，以及手边可得之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools laid out within reach on a workbench, ready for the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：工具摆在手边的工作台上，等着手去拿。

branches.en: a ready yes before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题未完就答应的 yes

branches.en: a task finished without effort
clean water waiting in a tap
branches.cn: 水龙头里随时可得的净水

branches.en: willing hands and easy work
easy to use and there when needed
branches.cn: 易于使用且需要时就在

intro.en: The word is ready plus the adverb ending -ly, built on a native adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是 ready 加副词词尾 -ly，建立在一条本族形容词上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 准备好的；乐意的；现成的；快要……的
definition_en: prepared for what is about to happen; willing to do something; available and already made; about to do something
core_image: 赛跑前蹲在起跑线、只等枪响的姿势
scene: 起跑线上，运动员蹲好姿势，只等一声枪响。The team was ready to leave at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 ready 是「准备好的」（第 1 个义项：已完成准备）；句意为队伍准备好在黎明出发。画面里可留意：起跑线上的蹲姿、绷紧的肌肉、等枪响的静默。

pos.zh: 准备好的；乐意的；现成的；快要……的

derivatives.zh: ready 加 -ly，指乐意地、容易地
ready 加 -ness，指准备就绪、乐意
ready 与 made 复合，指现成的
all 与 ready 复合，指已经

senses.title: Prepared
senses.definition: prepared and fit for what is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 已作好准备、适于应对即将发生之事
senses.example: The team was ready to leave at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍准备好在黎明出发。
senses.why: Old English ræde meant prepared, and the adjective still describes the state of being set for action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ræde 意为准备好，这个形容词至今描述「已为行动就位」的状态。

senses.title: Willing
senses.definition: willing and inclined to do something
senses.definitionCN: 愿意并有做某事的意思
senses.example: She is always ready to listen.
senses.exampleCN: 她总是乐意倾听。
senses.why: A person prepared to act is also prepared to say yes, so ready took on the sense of willing.
senses.whyCN: 准备好行动的人，也准备好答应，于是 ready 有了「乐意」的意思。

senses.title: Available and made
senses.definition: already made and available for use without further work
senses.definitionCN: 已经做好、无需再加工即可使用
senses.example: He bought a ready-made suit.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一套现成的西装。
senses.why: What has been prepared in advance is ready to use at once, and ready-made names exactly such goods.
senses.whyCN: 预先准备好的东西可以立刻使用，ready-made 正命名这类商品。

senses.title: About to do
senses.definition: on the point of doing something, used with to and a verb
senses.definitionCN: 即将做某事，与 to 和动词连用
senses.example: The kettle is ready to boil.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶快要烧开了。
senses.why: When the preparation is complete, the action can begin at once, so ready to do came to mean about to do.
senses.whyCN: 准备一旦完成，动作便可立刻开始，于是 ready to do 引申为「即将做」。

intro.en: Ready is a native English adjective from Old English ræde, prepared, related to rædan, to arrange or advise; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: ready 是英语本族形容词，来自古英语 ræde（准备好的），与 rædan（安排、劝告）相关；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Ræde meant prepared or fit, of a person or thing made ready for use.
items.cn: ræde 意为准备好的或合用的，指人或物已被安排得可用。

items.en: The adjective is tied to rædan, to arrange or advise, since preparing is a kind of arranging.
items.cn: 这个形容词与 rædan（安排、劝告）相连，因为准备就是一种安排。

items.en: Middle English ready kept the sense of prepared and added the sense of willing.
items.cn: 中古英语 ready 保留「准备好」之意，并加上「乐意」之意。

items.en: Goods made in advance were called ready-made, because they needed no further work before use.
items.cn: 预先做好的商品被称为 ready-made，因为它们使用前无需再加工。

items.en: Modern English uses ready for preparation, willingness, goods in stock, and the point of beginning an action.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ready 指准备、意愿、现货，以及动作即将开始。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers ready forms and one confusable word; the near-meaning group gathers words for being prepared and willing.
note.cn: 形近组收 ready 的形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示准备好与乐意的词。

entries.definition: Able to be used or obtained.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as prepared, then covers willingness, goods in stock, and the moment before an action.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「准备好」开始，随后涵盖意愿、现货，以及动作开始前的那一刻。

normal.en: Ready and readily are the same root: one is the state, the other the manner.
normal.cn: ready 与 readily 同根：一个是状态，一个是方式。

normal.en: Be ready for a test is to be prepared before it starts.
normal.cn: be ready for a test 就是在考试开始前做好准备。

normal.en: Be ready to help is to be willing to help.
normal.cn: be ready to help 就是乐意帮忙。

normal.en: Ready-made clothes need no fitting or sewing before you wear them.
normal.cn: ready-made 衣服不必量身或缝制就能穿。

normal.en: The kettle is ready to boil means it is about to boil.
normal.cn: 「The kettle is ready to boil」意为水壶快开了。

abstract.en: To be ready is to hold your energy at the edge of action.
abstract.cn: ready 就是把力量停在行动的边缘。

abstract.en: Readiness is invisible, but it decides how fast the visible begins.
abstract.cn: 准备看不见，却决定看得见的开始有多快。

abstract.en: What is ready-made saves time but carries another person's choices.
abstract.cn: 现成之物省下时间，却带着别人的选择。

examples.en: The team was ready to leave at dawn.
examples.cn: 队伍准备好在黎明出发。

examples.en: She is always ready to listen.
examples.cn: 她总是乐意倾听。

examples.en: He bought a ready-made suit.
examples.cn: 他买了一套现成的西装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「起跑线前的蹲姿」——只等枪响，记住 ready 是准备好的、乐意的。

root: 古英语 rædan（安排、劝告）→ ræde（准备好的）→ 英语 ready；同族有 readily、readiness、ready-made、already。

sensesIntro.en: The core is prepared; the senses divide into being set for action, being willing, being made in advance, and being about to act.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「已准备好」；义项分为为行动就位、乐意、预先做好，以及即将行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner crouched at the starting line, muscles tight, waiting for the gun.
core.cn: 核心意象：起跑线上蹲好的赛跑者，肌肉绷紧，只等枪响。

branches.en: a runner crouched at the line
branches.cn: 蹲在起跑线上的赛跑者

branches.en: a hand already raised to help
branches.cn: 已经举起准备帮忙的手

branches.en: a suit taken off the rack
a kettle trembling before the boil
branches.cn: 沸腾前微微颤动的水壶

branches.en: a body prepared and a mind willing
branches.cn: 准备好的身体与乐意的心

intro.en: The word is native, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词为本族词，其词族由英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 真实的；真正的；实际的；十足的
definition_en: actually existing and not imagined; genuine and not false; practical rather than theoretical; complete or utter, used for emphasis
core_image: 照片旁边的实物带着可以触摸的质地
scene: 桌上摆着一张照片和一枚同样的果子，果子拿在手里沉甸甸的。The painting looks real enough to touch.
sceneCN: 这里 real 是「真实的」（第 1 个义项：实际存在、非想象）；句意为这幅画逼真得仿佛可以触摸。画面里可留意：照片与实物、手中沉甸甸的果子。

pos.zh: 真实的；真正的；实际的；十足的

derivatives.zh: real 加 -ly，指真正地、确实
real 加 -ity，指现实、真实性
real 加 -istic，指现实的、逼真的
real 加 -ize，指意识到、实现

senses.title: Actually existing
senses.definition: actually existing in the world, not imagined or invented
senses.definitionCN: 确实存在于世上，而非想象或虚构
senses.example: The painting looks real enough to touch.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画逼真得仿佛可以触摸。
senses.why: Real comes from Latin res, a thing, so the adjective first marks what is a thing and not a mere image.
senses.whyCN: real 来自拉丁语 res（事物），因此这个形容词首先标记「是事物而非单纯影像」的东西。

senses.title: Genuine
senses.definition: genuine and not false, imitation or counterfeit
senses.definitionCN: 真的，而非虚假、仿制或伪造
senses.example: Is that a real diamond or a copy?
senses.exampleCN: 那是真钻石还是仿制品？
senses.why: A thing that truly exists can be told apart from a copy, so real came to mean genuine rather than fake.
senses.whyCN: 真正存在之物能与仿制品区分，于是 real 引申为「真的」而非假的。

senses.title: Practical
senses.definition: concerned with actual conditions rather than theory or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 关涉实际状况，而非理论或想象
senses.example: We need a real solution, not another promise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要实际的解决办法，而不是又一个承诺。
senses.why: What exists as a thing also exists in practice, so real extended from reality to practical effectiveness.
senses.whyCN: 作为事物存在的东西也在实践中存在，于是 real 从「现实」扩展到「实际有效」。

senses.title: Complete, for emphasis
senses.definition: used informally to emphasize a quality, often a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于强调某种性质，常为负面
senses.example: That was a real mess.
senses.exampleCN: 那真是一团糟。
senses.why: In casual speech the word for what truly exists became a general intensifier, marking something as fully and unmistakably so.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，表示「真正存在」的词变成一般强调词，标记某物完全且不容置疑地如此。

intro.en: Real comes from Latin realis, belonging to res, a thing; English borrowed it to mark what exists as a thing rather than as an image or a word.
intro.cn: real 来自拉丁语 realis，意为属于 res（事物）的；英语借它来标记「作为事物存在」而非影像或词语的东西。

items.en: Res meant a thing, a matter or a fact, the plainest word for what exists.
items.cn: res 意为事物、事情或事实，是表示「存在之物」最朴素的词。

items.en: Realis meant belonging to a thing, and it described what has actual existence.
items.cn: realis 意为属于事物的，形容具有实际存在的东西。

items.en: English took realis as real, setting what is real against what is imagined or copied.
items.cn: 英语把 realis 借作 real，把真实之物与想象或仿制之物相对。

items.en: Because a real thing is not a copy, the word grew to mean genuine, and then practical rather than theoretical.
items.cn: 由于真实之物不是复制品，这个词引申为「真正的」，再引申为「实际的」而非理论的。

items.en: Modern English uses real for existence, genuineness, practical effect, and informal emphasis.
items.cn: 现代英语用 real 指存在、真实、实际效果，以及口语中的强调。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on real; the near-meaning group gathers words for what truly exists or is genuine.
note.cn: 形近组收由 real 构成的形式；近义组收表示真实存在或名副其实的词。

entries.definition: To become aware of, or to make real.

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a thing that exists, then marks what is not a copy, what works in practice, and what is fully so.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「存在的事物」开始，随后标记「不是复制品」、在实践中有效，以及完全如此。

normal.en: Real comes from res, a thing, so real marks what is a thing and not just an image.
normal.cn: real 来自 res（事物），因此它标记「是事物而不只是影像」的东西。

normal.en: A real diamond and a copy look alike but only one is a thing of its own.
normal.cn: 真钻石与仿制品看起来一样，但只有一个是自身之物。

normal.en: Real life is life as it actually happens, outside stories.
normal.cn: real life 是故事之外实际发生的生活。

normal.en: A real problem is one that must actually be solved.
normal.cn: a real problem 是真正必须解决的问题。

normal.en: In speech, a real mess simply means a very great mess.
normal.cn: 在口语中，a real mess 只是指一团很大的糟。

abstract.en: The real is what remains when no one is looking.
abstract.cn: 真实，是无人观看时仍然存在的东西。

abstract.en: To call something real is to say it can be tested, touched or suffered.
abstract.cn: 称某物 real，是说它可以被检验、触摸或承受。

abstract.en: Real and imagined are not opposites in value, only in origin.
abstract.cn: 真实与想象在价值上并非对立，只在来源上不同。

examples.en: The painting looks real enough to touch.
examples.cn: 这幅画逼真得仿佛可以触摸。

examples.en: Is that a real diamond or a copy?
examples.cn: 那是真钻石还是仿制品？

examples.en: We need a real solution, not another promise.
examples.cn: 我们需要实际的解决办法，而不是又一个承诺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞尔」——照片旁的实物沉甸甸，摸得着，记住 real 是真实的、真正的。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis（属于事物的）→ 英语 real；同族有 really、reality、realistic、realize。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a thing that exists; the senses divide into actual existence, genuineness, practical effect, and emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「存在的事物」；义项分为实际存在、真正的、实际有效，以及强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a photograph beside the object itself, the object heavy in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：照片旁边就是实物，实物拿在手里沉甸甸的。

branches.en: an object heavier than its photo
a diamond that cuts glass
a solution that actually works
a thoroughly hopeless mess
what exists and what is not fake

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes and one negative prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由英语后缀与一个否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin res, a thing, and realis, belonging to a thing, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res（事物）与 realis（属于事物的）是有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 现实的；逼真的；可行的
definition_en: seeing things as they actually are and acting accordingly; looking or sounding like real life; achievable in practice
core_image: 画布上的静物与桌边实物几乎分不清
scene: 画布上的静物光影细腻，几乎与桌边的实物难以分辨。Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
sceneCN: 这里 realistic 是「现实的」（第 1 个义项：看清实际、不空想）；句意为她的旅行计划现实而省钱。画面里可留意：细腻的光影、几乎分不清的实物与画。

derivatives.zh: realistic 的词根，指真实的
real 加 -ism，指现实主义
real 加 -ist，指现实主义者
un- 与 realistic 复合，指不切实际的

senses.title: Seeing things as they are
senses.definition: judging situations by what is actually true and possible rather than by wishful thinking
senses.definitionCN: 按实际真实与可能来判断情况，而非凭一厢情愿
senses.example: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。
senses.why: Realistic adds the suffix -istic to real, so it describes a mind that keeps its eye on what actually exists.
senses.whyCN: realistic 在 real 后加后缀 -istic，因此它描述始终盯着实际存在的现实的心智。

senses.title: Looking like real life
senses.definition: represented so faithfully that it looks or sounds like real life
senses.definitionCN: 表现得太忠实，以致看起来或听起来像真实生活
senses.example: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。
senses.why: Art that copies what truly exists is called realistic, because its standard is the real thing outside the frame.
senses.whyCN: 摹写真实存在之物的艺术被称为 realistic，因为它的标准是画框之外的真实之物。

senses.title: Achievable
senses.definition: of a goal or expectation, possible to reach within real limits
senses.definitionCN: 指目标或期望在真实限度内可以达到
senses.example: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。
senses.why: A goal shaped by what is actually possible rather than by desire alone is described as realistic.
senses.whyCN: 按实际可能而非单凭愿望设定的目标，被称为 realistic。

intro.en: Realistic is English real with the suffix -istic, a learned ending that came through Latin from Greek; it describes what follows the real.
intro.cn: realistic 是英语 real 加上后缀 -istic，这个词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语；它描述合乎真实之物。

items.en: Res meant a thing, and realis meant belonging to a thing, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: res 意为事物，realis 意为属于事物的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: English borrowed real to mark what exists rather than what is imagined.
items.cn: 英语借入 real，用来标记存在之物而非想象之物。

items.en: The ending -istic came through Latin from Greek -istikos and forms adjectives of tendency or style.
items.cn: 词尾 -istic 经拉丁语来自希腊语 -istikos，构成表示倾向或风格的形容词。

items.en: The word first described art that copies life, then spread to plans and judgments that accept real limits.
items.cn: 这个词先描述摹写生活的艺术，随后扩展到接受真实限度的计划与判断。

items.en: Modern English uses realistic for practical judgment, lifelike representation, and reachable goals.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realistic 指务实的判断、逼真的表现与可达成的目标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for practical judgment and lifelike quality.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示务实判断与逼真品质的词。

entries.definition: To become aware of or make real.
A style that shows life as it is.
Concerned with doing rather than theory.

normalIntro.en: The word applies real in three directions: a mind that faces facts, an image that copies life, and a goal that respects limits.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把 real 用在三个方向：面对事实的心智、摹写生活的影像，以及尊重限度的目标。

normal.en: Realistic is real plus -istic, so it describes whatever keeps close to the real.
normal.cn: realistic 是 real 加 -istic，描述贴近真实之物。

normal.en: A realistic plan accepts what time and money actually allow.
normal.cn: 现实的计划接受时间与金钱的实际限度。

normal.en: A realistic painting copies light and shape so well that the eye is fooled.
normal.cn: 逼真的画把光与形摹得极像，以致骗过眼睛。

normal.en: Be realistic about a job means not expecting more than it can give.
normal.cn: be realistic about a job 意为不对它期望过高。

normal.en: Unrealistic is its direct opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unrealistic 是它的直接反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: To be realistic is to measure desire against possibility.
abstract.cn: 现实，就是用可能性来量愿望。

abstract.en: A realistic image is convincing because it obeys the same rules as the eye.
abstract.cn: 逼真的影像之所以可信，因为它遵守与眼睛相同的规则。

abstract.en: Realism is not pessimism; it is the refusal to subtract facts.
abstract.cn: 现实主义不是悲观，而是拒绝把事实减掉。

examples.en: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
examples.cn: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。

examples.en: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
examples.cn: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。

examples.en: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
examples.cn: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞丽斯提克」——画得像真的一样，计划也量力而行，记住 realistic 是现实的、逼真的。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → 英语 real + 后缀 -istic → realistic；同族有 realism、realist、unrealistic。

sensesIntro.en: The core is closeness to the real; the senses divide into practical judgment, lifelike representation, and achievable goals.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「贴近真实」；义项分为务实判断、逼真表现与可达成目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a still-life painting whose light and shadow almost cannot be told from the objects beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅静物画，光影几乎无法与桌边实物分辨。

branches.en: a plan that fits the budget
a painted apple the eye tries to bite
branches.cn: 逼真得让眼睛想去咬的画中苹果

branches.en: a goal set where feet can reach
facts accepted and goals kept reachable
branches.cn: 接受事实与保持目标可达

branches.en: an image true to life and a plan true to means
branches.cn: 忠于生活的影像与忠于财力的计划

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with a learned suffix, and its family spreads across art, thought and practice.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加学术词尾，其词族分布在艺术、思想与实践之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin res, a thing, and realis, belonging to a thing, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res（事物）与 realis（属于事物的）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a style showing life as it is

definition_zh: 现实；实际情况；真实性
definition_en: the state of things as they actually exist; the quality of being real rather than imagined; the facts of a situation
core_image: 清晨菜市场里嘈杂而实实在在的景象
scene: 清晨的菜市场人声嘈杂，泥水沾在菜叶上，一切都实实在在。The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
sceneCN: 这里 reality 是「现实」（第 1 个义项：实际存在的情形）；句意为这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。画面里可留意：嘈杂的市场、沾泥的菜叶、忙碌的人群。

derivatives.zh: reality 的词根，指真实的
real 加 -istic，指现实的、逼真的
real 加 -ize，指意识到、实现
un- 与 reality 复合，指不真实、虚幻

senses.title: The world as it exists
senses.definition: the state of things as they actually exist, including what is unpleasant or unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 事物实际存在的情形，包括不愉快或出乎意料之处
senses.example: The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。
senses.why: Reality is real plus -ity, so it names the condition of being a thing that exists, not a wish or a picture.
senses.whyCN: reality 是 real 加 -ity，命名「作为存在之物的状态」，而非愿望或画面。

senses.title: Genuineness
senses.definition: the quality of being genuine, true or actual rather than imagined
senses.definitionCN: 真正、真实或实际而非想象的性质
senses.example: The documentary blurs the line between reality and fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片模糊了真实与虚构的界限。
senses.why: The same noun can point at the quality itself: how much of the real is in a thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可指向性质本身：一物之中含有多少真实。

senses.title: Real life on screen
senses.definition: used as a modifier for programmes that show ordinary people in unscripted situations
senses.definitionCN: 用作定语，指展示普通人在无脚本情境中的节目
senses.example: Reality TV has changed what audiences expect from television.
senses.exampleCN: 真人秀改变了观众对电视的期待。
senses.why: Television borrowed the word for shows that claim to record real life rather than act it out.
senses.whyCN: 电视借用了这个词，指声称记录真实生活而非表演的节目。

intro.en: Reality is real with the Latin noun ending -ity, and its remote source is Latin res, a thing; it names the condition of being real.
intro.cn: reality 是 real 加拉丁名词词尾 -ity，其更早来源是拉丁语 res（事物）；它命名「真实的状况」。

items.en: Res meant a thing or a fact, the plain word for what exists.
items.cn: res 意为事物或事实，是「存在之物」的朴素说法。

items.en: Realitas meant the quality of being real, formed from realis with the noun ending -itas.
items.cn: realitas 意为真实的性质，由 realis 加名词词尾 -itas 构成。

items.en: English took the word as reality, keeping the sense of the way things actually stand.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 reality，保留「事物实际如何」的意思。

items.en: The word served for hard facts, then for television that claims to show life unscripted.
items.cn: 这个词先用于硬邦邦的事实，后用于声称展示无脚本生活的电视节目。

items.en: Modern English uses reality for the actual world, for genuineness, and for real-life television.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reality 指实际世界、真实性与真人生活类电视。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fact and actual existence.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示事实与实际存在的词。

entries.definition: The state of existing in fact.

normalIntro.en: The word names the condition of being real, then the hard facts of a situation, then television that claims to show life as it is.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词命名「真实的状况」，再指处境的硬事实，最后指声称展示真实生活的电视。

normal.en: Reality is real plus -ity, the noun for being real.
normal.cn: reality 是 real 加 -ity，表示「真实」的名词。

normal.en: In reality is the phrase for saying what actually happens, as opposed to what seems to.
normal.cn: in reality 是用来说实际发生什么、而非看似如何的短语。

normal.en: Face reality means to accept facts you would rather avoid.
normal.cn: face reality 意为接受你宁愿回避的事实。

normal.en: A dream becomes a reality when it stops being only imagined.
normal.cn: 梦想 stop 只是想象时，就成了现实。

normal.en: Reality TV claims to record ordinary life without a script.
normal.cn: reality TV 声称无脚本地记录普通生活。

abstract.en: Reality is what does not disappear when you stop believing in it.
abstract.cn: 现实，是你不再相信时也不会消失的东西。

abstract.en: Every plan meets reality at the point where it must change.
abstract.cn: 每个计划都在必须改变之处遇上现实。

abstract.en: The word reality is often used to end an argument that facts have already won.
abstract.cn: reality 一词常被用来终结一场事实早已获胜的争论。

examples.en: The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
examples.cn: 这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。

examples.en: The documentary blurs the line between reality and fiction.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片模糊了真实与虚构的界限。

examples.en: Reality TV has changed what audiences expect from television.
examples.cn: 真人秀改变了观众对电视的期待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞阿勒提」——菜市场的泥水与吆喝都实实在在，记住 reality 是现实、真实性。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → realitas → 英语 reality；同族有 real、realistic、realize、unreality。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the condition of being real; the senses divide into the actual world, genuineness, and real-life television.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「真实的状况」；义项分为实际世界、真实性，以及真人生活类电视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a noisy morning market, mud on the vegetables, everything solid and unposed.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨嘈杂的菜市场，菜叶上沾着泥，一切都实实在在、未经摆拍。

branches.en: a muddy market at dawn
a documentary without a script
a reality show filming ordinary people
the actual world and the quality of being actual
branches.cn: 实际世界与「实际」这一性质

branches.en: life as lived and life as televised
branches.cn: 被经历的生活与被 televised 的生活

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with a noun ending, and its family spreads through thought, art and media.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加名词词尾，其词族分布在思想、艺术与媒体之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin res, realis and realitas are the recorded sources of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res、realis 与 realitas 是这个词族有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: the state of not being real

definition_zh: 意识到；实现；变卖
definition_en: to become aware of something one did not notice before; to make a plan or aim actually happen; to sell property and receive money for it
core_image: 走到半路忽然停住、回头的神情
scene: 走到半路，忽然想起钥匙还在桌上，脚步猛地停住。She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
sceneCN: 这里 realize 是「意识到」（第 1 个义项：忽然明白某事）；句意为她忽然意识到门没锁。画面里可留意：停住的脚步、回头的神情、头顶亮起的灯。

derivatives.zh: realize 的词根，指真实的
real 加 -ity，指现实
realize 加 -ation，指认识、实现
un- 与 realized 复合，指未实现的

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become aware of something that was not noticed or understood before
senses.definitionCN: 察觉此前未注意或未理解之事
senses.example: She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 她忽然意识到门没锁。
senses.why: To realize is to make something real in the mind, to bring a fact into awareness where it was not before.
senses.whyCN: to realize 就是在心里使某物变为真实，把事实带到此前没有的觉察之中。

senses.title: To make happen
senses.definition: to turn a plan, aim or hope into actual fact
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、目标或希望变成实际事实
senses.example: He worked hard to realize his dream of opening a shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他努力工作以实现开一家店的梦想。
senses.why: The other direction of the same image is to make a thing real in the world, not only in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象的另一方向，是使某物在世界上真实存在，而不只在心里。

senses.title: To sell for money
senses.definition: to sell property or goods and receive money for them
senses.definitionCN: 卖掉财产或货物并换成钱
senses.example: The company realized a large sum from the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 公司从事这笔买卖中获得了一大笔钱。
senses.why: Property sold becomes money actually in hand, so the word took on the commercial sense of turning an asset into cash.
senses.whyCN: 售出的财产变成手里实实在在的钱，于是这个词有了「把资产换成现金」的商业义。

intro.en: Realize is real plus the verb ending -ize, modelled on Latin realis; it means to make real, whether in the mind or in the world.
intro.cn: realize 是 real 加动词词尾 -ize，仿拉丁语 realis 构成；意为「使真实」，无论在心中还是在世上。

items.en: Res meant a thing, and what is real is what belongs to things as they exist.
items.cn: res 意为事物，而真实之物就是属于实际存在之物的东西。

items.en: Realis meant belonging to a thing, and English real grew from it.
items.cn: realis 意为属于事物的，英语 real 由它而来。

items.en: The ending -ize forms verbs meaning to make or become, so real plus -ize is to make real.
items.cn: 词尾 -ize 构成意为「使……成为」的动词，因此 real 加 -ize 就是「使真实」。

items.en: One can make a fact real to the mind by realizing it, or make a plan real in the world by carrying it out.
items.cn: 人可以通过 realize 使事实在心智中变真，也可以通过执行使计划在世界上成真。

items.en: Modern English uses realize for awareness, for the completion of plans, and for turning property into money.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realize 指觉察、完成计划，以及把财产换成钱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of noticing, achieving and selling.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示察觉、达成与出售的动词。

entries.definition: The act of becoming aware or making real.
To see or become aware of.
To reach a goal by effort.
To carry out a promise or aim.

normalIntro.en: The verb has two directions: making something real in the mind, which is awareness, and making it real in the world, which is achievement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词有两个方向：在心里使某物变真，即觉察；在世上使某物成真，即实现。

normal.en: Realize is real plus -ize, so it means to make real.
normal.cn: realize 是 real 加 -ize，意为「使真实」。

normal.en: To realize a fact is to make it real to your mind.
normal.cn: to realize 一个事实，就是让它在你心里变真。

normal.en: To realize a plan is to make it real in the world.
normal.cn: to realize 一个计划，就是让它在世上成真。

normal.en: Realize an asset is to turn property into money you can hold.
normal.cn: realize 一项资产，就是把财产变成手里能拿的钱。

normal.en: Realization is the noun, naming either the moment of awareness or the completion of a plan.
normal.cn: realization 是名词，或指觉察的那一刻，或指计划的完成。

abstract.en: We often realize too late what we already knew.
abstract.cn: 我们常常太晚才 realize 早已知道的事。

abstract.en: A dream realized changes the person who dreamed it.
abstract.cn: 被实现的梦想会改变做梦的人。

abstract.en: Awareness and achievement share one word because both make the invisible real.
abstract.cn: 觉察与成就共用一个词，因为两者都让看不见的变真。

examples.en: She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
examples.cn: 她忽然意识到门没锁。

examples.en: He worked hard to realize his dream of opening a shop.
examples.cn: 他努力工作以实现开一家店的梦想。

examples.en: The company realized a large sum from the sale.
examples.cn: 公司从事这笔买卖中获得了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「走到半路忽然停住」——想起钥匙还在桌上，记住 realize 是意识到、实现。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → 英语 real + 动词后缀 -ize → realize；同族有 reality、realization、unrealized。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making something real; the senses divide into awareness in the mind, achievement in the world, and cash from property.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使某物变真」；义项分为心中的觉察、世上的实现，以及财产换来的现金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps stopping halfway as a forgotten fact returns to mind.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚步走到半路停住，一件被忘记的事回到心里。

branches.en: a foot stopping on the stairs
a shop sign going up at last
a deed exchanged for money
a fact made real to the mind and a plan made real in the world
branches.cn: 心中变真的事实与世上成真的计划

branches.en: an aim completed and an asset converted
branches.cn: 完成的目标与变现的资产

intro.en: The word is real plus a verb ending, and its family spreads through awareness, achievement and property.
intro.cn: 这个词是 real 加动词词尾，其词族分布在觉察、成就与财产之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin res and realis are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res 与 realis 是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 真正地；确实；非常；真的吗
definition_en: in fact or truly; very, used as an intensifier; used in questions to express surprise or doubt
core_image: 放大镜下忽然看清的细微纹理
scene: 放大镜移过去，纸面上原本看不见的纹理一下子清楚了。I really enjoyed the concert last night.
sceneCN: 这里 really 是「非常」（第 2 个义项：加强语气）；句意为昨晚的音乐会我非常喜欢。画面里可留意：放大镜、被看清的纹理、纸面。

pos.zh: 真正地；确实；非常；真的吗

derivatives.zh: really 去掉 -ly，指真实的
real 加 -ity，指现实
real 加 -istic，指现实的、逼真的
real 加 -ize，指意识到、实现

senses.title: In fact
senses.definition: in fact, truly, in the way things actually are
senses.definitionCN: 事实上、真正地，按事物实际的样子
senses.example: Do you really mean what you said?
senses.exampleCN: 你真的是这个意思吗？
senses.why: Really is real with -ly, so in its first sense it says that something is so in fact, not merely in appearance.
senses.whyCN: really 是 real 加 -ly，因此它的第一个意思说某事事实上如此，而不只是表面上如此。

senses.title: Very
senses.definition: to a high degree, used to strengthen a word
senses.definitionCN: 达到很高程度，用于加强语气
senses.example: I really enjoyed the concert last night.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚的音乐会我非常喜欢。
senses.why: If a thing is really so, it is fully so, and that fullness became a general way of saying very.
senses.whyCN: 若一物真的是这样，它就是完全这样，而这种「完全」成了说「非常」的一般方式。

senses.title: Used to show surprise
senses.definition: used in questions or replies to express surprise, doubt or mild protest
senses.definitionCN: 用于疑问或回答，表示惊讶、怀疑或轻微反对
senses.example: Really? I never heard that before.
senses.exampleCN: 真的吗？我从没听说过。
senses.why: A speaker who asks whether something is truly so is often doubting it, so the word became a ready signal of surprise.
senses.whyCN: 问某事是否真的如此的人，往往是在怀疑，于是这个词成了现成的惊讶信号。

intro.en: Really is real plus the adverb ending -ly; real goes back through Latin realis to res, a thing.
intro.cn: really 是 real 加副词词尾 -ly；real 经拉丁语 realis 可追溯到 res（事物）。

items.en: Res meant a thing or a fact, the base of the whole family.
items.cn: res 意为事物或事实，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: English real marks what exists in fact rather than in image or word.
items.cn: 英语 real 标记事实上存在之物，而非影像或言辞。

items.en: The ending -ly turned real into really, meaning in fact or truly.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把 real 变成 really，意为事实上或真正地。

items.en: Because what is truly so is fully so, really weakened into a common word for very.
items.cn: 由于真正如此就是完全如此，really 弱化为表示「非常」的常用词。

items.en: Modern English uses really for truth, for emphasis, and for surprise in questions.
items.cn: 现代英语用 really 指真实、强调，以及疑问中的惊讶。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of truth and emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示真实与强调的副词。

normalIntro.en: The adverb moves from truth to emphasis to surprise: what is really so is fully so, and a question about it is often a doubt.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词从真实转到强调，再转到惊讶：真的如此就是完全如此，而对此提问往往就是怀疑。

normal.en: Really is real with -ly, so its oldest job is to say that something is so in fact.
normal.cn: really 是 real 加 -ly，它最古老的工作就是说明某事事实上如此。

normal.en: Really good means good to a high degree, stronger than quite good.
normal.cn: really good 指好到很高程度，比 quite good 更强。

normal.en: Not really is a soft way of saying no or only a little.
normal.cn: not really 是温和地说「不」或「只有一点」。

normal.en: Really? turns a statement into a question of doubt or surprise.
normal.cn: Really? 把陈述变成怀疑或惊讶的追问。

normal.en: Really and truly appear together when a speaker wants to insist.
normal.cn: really and truly 连用，是说话人想要强调之时。

abstract.en: Really asks whether the surface matches the depth.
abstract.cn: really 问的是表面是否与内里相符。

abstract.en: To say really is to claim that no illusion is left.
abstract.cn: 说 really，就是声称没有留下任何幻觉。

abstract.en: A word that began with truth ended as a tool for emphasis.
abstract.cn: 一个从真实开始的词，最终成了强调的工具。

examples.en: Do you really mean what you said?
examples.cn: 你真的是这个意思吗？

examples.en: I really enjoyed the concert last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚的音乐会我非常喜欢。

examples.en: Really? I never heard that before.
examples.cn: 真的吗？我从没听说过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「放大镜下看清纹理」——原来真的如此，记住 really 是真正地、确实、非常。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → 英语 real + 副词后缀 -ly → really；同族有 real、reality、realistic、realize。

sensesIntro.en: The core is truth; the senses divide into in fact, a strong degree, and a marker of surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「真实」；义项分为事实上、很强的程度，以及惊讶的标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass revealing fine lines that were invisible a moment before.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜揭出片刻前还看不见的细纹。

branches.en: a claim checked against the facts
a meal enjoyed to the full
a raised eyebrow at a strange claim
branches.cn: 听到怪说法时扬起的眉毛

branches.en: true in fact and true to a high degree
branches.cn: 事实上为真，且程度很高

branches.en: emphasis and the doubt that questions it
branches.cn: 强调与对它发问的怀疑

intro.en: The word is real plus the adverb ending -ly, with a Latin root behind it.
intro.cn: 这个词是 real 加副词词尾 -ly，其背后有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin res and realis are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res 与 realis 是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 领域；王国；界
definition_en: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest; a kingdom or country ruled by a monarch; a major division of the natural world
core_image: 地图上由边界线围起的一片土地
scene: 地图摊在桌上，边界线把一片土地清清楚楚地围起来。The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
sceneCN: 这里 realm 是「领域」（第 1 个义项：某一活动或知识的范围）；句意为昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。画面里可留意：摊开的地图、清楚的边界线、围起的土地。

derivatives.zh: 与 realm 同源的拉丁词，指王室的
与 realm 同源的拉丁词，指政权、制度
与 realm 同源的拉丁词，指地区

senses.title: A field or area
senses.definition: a field or area of activity, knowledge or interest
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或兴趣的一个范围
senses.example: The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。
senses.why: A realm was first a territory with borders, and a field of study is also a territory with borders, so the word extended to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: realm 最初指有边界的领土，而一个研究领域也是有边界的领土，于是这个词扩展到知识。

senses.title: A kingdom
senses.definition: a country or kingdom ruled by a monarch
senses.definitionCN: 由君主统治的国家或王国
senses.example: The old realm was divided among three kings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老的王国被三位国王瓜分。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a land under a ruler, the territory that a king actually governs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「君主统治下的土地」，即国王实际治理的疆域。

senses.title: A division of nature
senses.definition: one of the great divisions of the natural world, such as animals, plants or fungi
senses.definitionCN: 自然世界的主要划分之一，如动物界、植物界或真菌界
senses.example: Fungi form a realm of their own, neither plant nor animal.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌自成—界，既非植物也非动物。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word for the largest divisions of living things, because each is a territory with its own borders.
senses.whyCN: 科学借这个词指生物最大的几大划分，因为每一界都是有自身边界的领土。

intro.en: Realm comes from Old French reaume, a kingdom, from Latin regimen, rule, and regere, to rule; English narrowed the spelling but kept the territory.
intro.cn: realm 来自古法语 reaume（王国），源于拉丁语 regimen（统治）与 regere（统治）；英语改变了拼写，却保留了「领土」之意。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or guide straight, and it is the source of regal, regime and region as well.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或引直，也是 regal、regime、region 的来源。

items.en: Regimen meant rule or government, the act by which a territory is held.
items.cn: regimen 意为统治或治理，是维系一片领土的行为。

items.en: Old French reaume named the kingdom itself, the land that a ruler governs.
items.cn: 古法语 reaume 命名王国本身，即统治者所治理的土地。

items.en: Middle English shortened the spelling toward realm but kept the sense of a ruled territory.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写缩短为 realm，但保留「被统治的领土」之意。

items.en: Modern English uses realm for a kingdom, for any bounded field of activity, and for a division of nature.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realm 指王国、任何有边界的活动领域，以及自然界的一大划分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same ruling root; the near-meaning group gathers words for territory and field.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「统治」词根的词；近义组收表示领土与范围的词。

entries.definition: Belonging to a king or queen.
A system or government of rule.
A country ruled by a king or queen.
entries.definitionCN: 由国王或女王统治的国家。

entries.definition: An area of activity or knowledge.
A branch of study or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或活动的一个分支。

entries.definition: A area of activity or influence.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a ruled territory, then becomes any bounded field, and finally a great division of nature.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「被统治的领土」开始，随后成为任何有边界的领域，最后成为自然界的一大划分。

normal.en: Realm, regal, regime and region all come from the Latin word for rule.
normal.cn: realm、regal、regime、region 都来自拉丁语中表示「统治」的词。

normal.en: A realm is a territory with borders, whether a kingdom or a field of study.
normal.cn: realm 是有边界的领土，可以是王国，也可以是研究领域。

normal.en: The realm of nature is a phrase for the whole living world.
normal.cn: the realm of nature 指整个生命世界的说法。

normal.en: Within the realm of is the phrase for saying what an idea belongs to.
normal.cn: within the realm of 是用来说明某观念属于哪个范围的短语。

normal.en: A realm can be expanded, as a kingdom adds land or a science adds subjects.
normal.cn: realm 可以扩展，正如王国增添土地、科学增添科目。

abstract.en: Every realm is made by the border drawn around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个 realm 都由围在它周围的边界造成。

abstract.en: To enter a new realm is to accept its rules.
abstract.cn: 进入一个新的领域，就是接受它的规则。

abstract.en: The realm of the possible is wider than the realm of the permitted.
abstract.cn: 可能的领域比被允许的领域更宽。

examples.en: The realm of insects is far larger than most people imagine.
examples.cn: 昆虫的领域远比多数人想象的大。

examples.en: The old realm was divided among three kings.
examples.cn: 这个古老的王国被三位国王瓜分。

examples.en: Fungi form a realm of their own, neither plant nor animal.
examples.cn: 真菌自成一界，既非植物也非动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞尔姆」——地图上一圈边界围起的土地，记住 realm 是领域、王国。

root: 拉丁语 regere（统治）→ regimen（统治）→ 古法语 reaume → 中古英语 realm；同族有 regal、regime、region。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bordered territory; the senses divide into a kingdom, a field of activity, and a division of nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有边界的领土」；义项分为王国、活动领域，以及自然界的一大划分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretch of land enclosed by a clearly drawn border on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一片被清楚画出的边界围住的土地。

branches.en: a subject with its own borders
a king's land on an old map
fungi set apart from plants and animals
a field of study and a kingdom, both bordered
branches.cn: 研究领域与王国，都有边界

branches.en: a kingdom of land and a kingdom of living things
branches.cn: 土地的王國与生物的王國

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from a Latin root, and its family spreads across rule, place and knowledge.
intro.cn: 这个词是源自拉丁词根的法语借词，其词族分布在统治、地方与知识之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere, to rule, and regimen, rule, are the recorded sources of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere（统治）与 regimen（统治）是这个词族有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a realm ruled by a king

definition_zh: 后部；后面的；抚养；饲养；抬起
definition_en: the back part of something; at or toward the back; to bring up a child; to breed animals; to raise something, especially the head
core_image: 马车后轮与车厢尾部
scene: 马车停在院门口，车尾对着台阶，后轮还沾着泥。He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
sceneCN: 这里 rear 是「后部」（第 1 个义项：某物的后面部分）；句意为马车停在院门口，他转身朝房子后部走去。画面里可留意：马车尾部、后轮上的泥、台阶。

derivatives.zh: rear 加 -ward，指朝后的
rear 加 -most，指最后面的
rear 加 -ing，指抚养、饲养

senses.title: The back part
senses.definition: the back part of a building, vehicle or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、车辆或物体的后面部分
senses.example: He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他转身朝房子后部走去。
senses.why: The back sense came from Old French riere and Latin retro, both meaning behind, and it names the part that lies at the back.
senses.whyCN: 「后面」之义来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，二者都意为「在后」，它命名位于后方的部分。

senses.title: At the back
senses.definition: located at or toward the back
senses.definitionCN: 位于后方或朝后的
senses.example: The rear window was steamed up with rain.
senses.exampleCN: 后窗被雨水蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The adjective simply applies the back sense to a noun, marking the part that sits behind the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「后面」的意思用于名词，标记位于其余部分之后的那一部分。

senses.title: To bring up a child
senses.definition: to care for a child until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子直到其长大
senses.example: She reared three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old English ræran, to raise, and raising a child is lifting it toward adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，即古英语 ræran（抬起），抚养孩子就是把他托向成年。

senses.title: To breed animals
senses.definition: to keep and breed animals or grow plants
senses.definitionCN: 饲养并繁殖动物，或栽培植物
senses.example: The farm rears sheep for wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养羊取毛。
senses.why: Animals are also raised up from young to grown, so the raising sense extends from children to livestock.
senses.whyCN: 动物也是从幼小被养到长成，于是「抬起」之义从孩子扩展到牲畜。

senses.title: To raise the head
senses.definition: to lift something, especially the head, often used of an animal or of something emerging
senses.definitionCN: 抬起某物，尤指头，常用于动物或某物冒现
senses.example: The horse reared its head at the sound.
senses.exampleCN: 马听到声音抬起了头。
senses.why: The oldest sense of ræran is to raise physically, and this literal lifting survives in phrases such as rear its head.
senses.whyCN: ræran 最古老的意思就是实际抬起，这种字面抬起保留在 rear its head 等说法中。

intro.en: Rear is really two words that came to share one spelling: the back sense from Old French riere and Latin retro, and the raising sense from Old English ræran.
intro.cn: rear 其实是两个词共用一个拼写：表示「后面」的义项来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，表示「抬起」的义项来自古英语 ræran。

items.en: Riere meant behind, and it named the back part of a place or a formation.
items.cn: riere 意为在后，命名一处地方或队列的后部。

items.en: Retro meant backward, and it stands behind the back sense of rear as well as words like retrograde.
items.cn: retro 意为向后，它支撑着 rear 的「后面」义以及与 retrograde 等词的关联。

items.en: Ræran meant to raise or bring up, and it is the source of the farming and family senses.
items.cn: ræran 意为抬起或养育，是饲养与抚养义项的来源。

items.en: The two words came to share the spelling rear, so one form now carries both the back and the raising.
items.cn: 两个词共用 rear 这一拼写，于是一个形式同时承载「后面」与「抬起」。

items.en: Modern English uses rear for the back, for what is behind, for bringing up children and animals, and for lifting the head.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rear 指后部、后面的、抚养孩子与饲养动物，以及抬起头。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and one easily confused word; the near-meaning group gathers words for the back and for raising.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与一个易混词；近义组收表示后方与抚养的词。

entries.definition: To care for and encourage growth.

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries two histories: the back of a thing, and the act of raising a thing up.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拼写承载两段历史：一物的后部，以及把一物抬起来的行为。

normal.en: Rear and rare look alike, but rare means uncommon while rear means the back or to raise.
normal.cn: rear 与 rare 形近，但 rare 意为罕见，rear 意为后部或抬起。

normal.en: The rear of a car is the part behind the driver.
normal.cn: 车的 rear 是司机后面的部分。

normal.en: To rear children is to bring them up, not to put them at the back.
normal.cn: to rear children 是抚养他们，不是把他们放到后面。

normal.en: To rear cattle is to keep and breed them on a farm.
normal.cn: to rear cattle 是在农场饲养并繁殖牛。

normal.en: A problem rears its head when it suddenly appears.
normal.cn: 问题 rears its head，就是它突然冒出来。

abstract.en: The back and the act of raising share a spelling but not a history.
abstract.cn: 「后部」与「抬起」共用一个拼写，却不共有一段历史。

abstract.en: What is reared is brought from behind to the front of life.
abstract.cn: 被抚养之物，是从后头被带到生命的前台。

abstract.en: To look to the rear is to remember where you came from.
abstract.cn: 看向 rear，就是回望你从何处来。

examples.en: He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
examples.cn: 他转身朝房子后部走去。

examples.en: The rear window was steamed up with rain.
examples.cn: 后窗被雨水蒙上了水汽。

examples.en: She reared three children on her own.
examples.cn: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「马车尾部」——后轮沾着泥，记住 rear 是后部、后面的；也指抚养、抬起。

root: 「后部」义：古法语 riere / 拉丁语 retro（在后）；「抬起、抚养」义：古英语 ræran（抬起）。同族有 rearward、rearmost。

sensesIntro.en: One form holds two histories; the senses divide into the back part, the back position, bringing up the young, breeding animals, and lifting the head.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个形式承载两段历史；义项分为后部、后面的位置、抚养幼者、饲养动物，以及抬起头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the back wheels and tail of a carriage standing at a gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在院门口的马车后轮与车尾。

branches.en: the tail end of a carriage
a window at the back of a house
a mother raising three children
sheep bred for wool on a farm
branches.cn: 农场里为取毛而饲养的羊

branches.en: a horse lifting its head at a sound

intro.en: The word joins two origins under one spelling, and its family is built with English suffixes and phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词在同一拼写下汇合两个来源，其词族由英语后缀与短语构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin retro, backward, is the recorded source of the back sense; the raising sense is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 retro（向后）是「后面」义有记录可考的来源；「抬起」义则是古英语本族。

items.meaning: to stand on the hind legs

definition_zh: 原因；理由；理性；道理；推理；说服
definition_en: a cause or justification for something; the power of logical thought; good sense or fairness; to think logically; to persuade someone by argument
core_image: 白板上一条从问题连到答案的清晰线
scene: 白板上，一条线从问题连到答案，每一步都标得清楚。There is no reason to doubt her story.
sceneCN: 这里 reason 是「理由」（第 1 个义项：支持某判断的根据）；句意为没有理由怀疑她的说法。画面里可留意：白板上连到答案的线、标清楚的每一步。

senses.title: A cause or justification
senses.definition: a cause or explanation that justifies something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供根据的原因或解释
senses.example: There is no reason to doubt her story.
senses.exampleCN: 没有理由怀疑她的说法。
senses.why: Latin ratio meant a reckoning, and a reason is the reckoning that stands behind a claim or an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ratio 意为计算，而理由就是支撑一个说法或事件的那笔「计算」。

senses.title: The power of logical thought
senses.definition: the human power of thinking logically and drawing conclusions
senses.definitionCN: 进行逻辑思考并得出结论的心智能力
senses.example: Reason separates a careful judge from a rash one.
senses.exampleCN: 理性把谨慎的判断者与草率者区分开来。
senses.why: The same reckoning that gives a reason for a claim is also the faculty that performs the reckoning, so reason names the mind's calculating power.
senses.whyCN: 支撑说法的计算，也是完成计算的能力，因此 reason 指心智的计算力。

senses.title: Good sense or fairness
senses.definition: good sense, fairness or what is right in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 良好判断、公平，或处境中正确之事
senses.example: There is reason in what she says, even if we disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话里有道理，即使我们不同意。
senses.why: What follows reason is felt as right and fair, so the word came to name the quality of being in accordance with good sense.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之事被感受为正确而公平，于是这个词也命名「合乎常理」的品质。

senses.title: To think logically
senses.definition: to think through facts and form a judgment by logic
senses.definitionCN: 梳理事实并用逻辑形成判断
senses.example: He reasoned that the letter must have been sent yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 他推断这封信一定是昨天寄出的。
senses.why: Reason as a verb is simply the mind doing what the noun names: reckoning from facts toward a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 作动词的 reason 就是心智做名词所指之事：从事实推算到结论。

senses.title: To persuade by argument
senses.definition: to persuade someone by presenting arguments rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过提出论据而非强力来说服某人
senses.example: She tried to reason with the angry customer.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着与愤怒的顾客讲道理。
senses.why: When reasoning is aimed at another person, the verb means to bring that person's mind into line through argument.
senses.whyCN: 当推理指向另一个人时，这个动词便指通过论证把对方的心拉到同一线上。

intro.en: Reason comes from Old French reisun, from Latin ratio, reckoning and reason, which itself comes from reri, to reckon or think.
intro.cn: reason 来自古法语 reisun，源于拉丁语 ratio（计算与理性），而 ratio 又来自 reri（计算、思考）。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon or think, the act behind every form of this family.
items.cn: reri 意为计算或思考，是整个词族背后的动作。

items.en: Ratio meant a reckoning and also the faculty of reason that makes reckoning possible.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算，也指使计算成为可能的理性能力。

items.en: Old French reisun carried the word to English with the sense of a cause and of good judgment.
items.cn: 古法语 reisun 把这个词带到英语，带着「原因」与「良好判断」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reason kept both the explanation and the thinking power, and added the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 reason 既保留解释，也保留思维能力，并加上了动词用法。

items.en: Modern English uses reason for causes, for the thinking power, for fairness, for logical argument, and for persuading.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reason 指原因、思维能力、公平、逻辑论证，以及说服。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same reckoning root; the near-meaning group gathers words for cause, logic and persuasion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「计算」词根的词；近义组收表示原因、逻辑与说服的词。

entries.definition: A reason for acting in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行动的理由。

normalIntro.en: The word is reckoning: it names the cause behind an event, the mind that reckons, the fairness that reckoning yields, and the acts of reasoning and persuading.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「计算」：它命名事件背后的原因、进行计算的心智、计算带来的公平，以及推理与说服的行为。

normal.en: Reason and ratio come from the same Latin word for reckoning.
normal.cn: reason 与 ratio 来自同一个表示「计算」的拉丁词。

normal.en: The reason for a thing is the explanation that stands behind it.
normal.cn: 一物的 reason，就是站在它背后的解释。

normal.en: Reason as a power is what lets a person follow an argument.
normal.cn: 作为能力的 reason，使人能够跟上论证。

normal.en: Within reason means inside the limits of what makes sense.
normal.cn: within reason 意为在合乎情理的限度之内。

normal.en: To reason with someone is to argue calmly rather than force them.
normal.cn: to reason with 某人，是平静论理而非强迫对方。

abstract.en: A reason is a bridge between a fact and a conclusion.
abstract.cn: reason 是事实与结论之间的一座桥。

abstract.en: Reason can be used to justify almost anything, which is why it needs honesty.
abstract.cn: 理性几乎可以为任何事辩护，因此它需要诚实。

abstract.en: To lose one's reason is to lose the bridge, not the world.
abstract.cn: 失去理智，是失去那座桥，而不是失去世界。

sceneCN: 这里 reasonable 是「公道的」（第 2 个义项：价格公平、不离谱）；句意为这家酒店的房间价格公道。画面里可留意：平衡的天平、停在正中的指针、价目牌。

pos.zh: 合理的；公道的；还算好的

senses.title: Sensible and fair
senses.definition: based on good reason and fair to those involved
senses.definitionCN: 基于充分理由，且对相关各方公平
senses.example: She gave a reasonable explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。
senses.why: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it describes what can be supported by reason and accepted as fair.
senses.whyCN: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，描述能被理由支持、并被接受为公平的事物。

senses.title: Fair in price
senses.definition: of a price, not too high and fair for what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 指价格不过高，与所提供之物相称
senses.example: The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店的房间价格公道。
senses.why: A price that reason can approve is one that is not excessive, so the word came to mean fair in price.
senses.whyCN: 理性能够认可的价格，就是不过分的价格，于是这个词引申为「价格公道」。

senses.title: Moderate and acceptable
senses.definition: of an amount, moderate but enough to be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 指数量适中但足以令人接受
senses.example: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.
senses.exampleCN: 完成这项工作有相当充裕的时间。
senses.why: What stays within reason is neither tiny nor excessive, so the word marks a moderate amount that still satisfies.
senses.whyCN: 合乎理性之物既不过小也不过量，因此这个词标记一个适中却仍令人满意的数量。

intro.en: Reasonable is reason plus the ending -able, meaning able to be supported by reason; reason itself goes back to Latin ratio.
intro.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加词尾 -able，意为能被理由支持的；reason 本身可追溯到拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning and reason, the standard against which a claim is judged.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算与理性，是评判一个说法的标准。

items.en: English reason carries both the cause behind a thing and the mind's power of judging.
items.cn: 英语 reason 既承载事物背后的原因，也承载心智的判断力。

items.en: The ending -able means able to be, so reason plus -able is able to be justified by reason.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 意为「能被……的」，因此 reason 加 -able 就是「能被理性证明的」。

items.en: A sum that reason approves is fair, and an amount that reason accepts is moderate.
items.cn: 理性认可的数额是公道的，理性接受的数量是适中的。

items.en: Modern English uses reasonable for fair judgment, fair prices, and moderate but acceptable amounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reasonable 指公平的判断、公道的价格，以及适中却可接受的数量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the reason root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fairness and moderation.
note.cn: 形近组收 reason 词根的词；近义组收表示公平与适中的词。

entries.definition: A cause or the thinking power.
Neither too much nor too little.

normalIntro.en: The word asks whether reason can approve: a fair judgment, a fair price, and a moderate amount all pass that test.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词问的是理性能否认可：公平的判断、公道的价格、适中的数量都能通过这一检验。

normal.en: Reasonable is reason plus -able, so it means able to be justified by reason.
normal.cn: reasonable 是 reason 加 -able，意为能被理性证明的。

normal.en: A reasonable price is one that does not ask too much.
normal.cn: 公道的价格，是不过分索价的价格。

normal.en: A reasonable explanation is one that holds together and is fair.
normal.cn: 合理的解释，是前后一致且公平的解释。

normal.en: Be reasonable about a delay means do not react with anger.
normal.cn: be reasonable about a delay 意为不要动怒。

normal.en: Unreasonable is the opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unreasonable 是反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: Reasonable is the meeting point of logic and fairness.
abstract.cn: reasonable 是逻辑与公平的交汇处。

abstract.en: What is reasonable to one person may still be too much for another.
abstract.cn: 对一个人合理的，对另一个人也许仍然过分。

abstract.en: To be reasonable is to leave room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 讲道理，就是给对方留下余地。

examples.en: She gave a reasonable explanation for the delay.
examples.cn: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。

examples.en: The hotel charges a reasonable price for the room.
examples.cn: 这家酒店的房间价格公道。

examples.en: There was a reasonable amount of time to finish the work.
examples.cn: 完成这项工作有相当充裕的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「天平停在正中」——两边重量相当，价格与道理都不过分，记住 reasonable 是合理的、公道的。

root: 拉丁语 reri（计算）→ ratio（理性）→ 古法语 reisun → 英语 reason + 后缀 -able → reasonable；同族有 reasonably、unreasonable。
